arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/how-it-works.md'
s=open(p).read()
a="the tool and its main argument (the command, the path, or the label)"
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,"the tool and its main argument (the command, the path, or the label). For a script of more than one line, the first line and the number of other lines")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
npx oxfmt --check docs >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
git add -A && git commit -q -m "feat: show a multi-line tool command as its first line and its length" -m "Heredocs and scripts read as one long run-on line in the 🔧 line (bash: python3 - <<'EOF' p='src/run.ts' s=open(p)...). Show the first line and '(+N lines)' instead; the result's group keeps the full arguments. Refs #46" && timeout 120 git push -q -u origin feat/46-multiline-commands 2>&1 | tail -1
timeout 120 gh pr create --title "feat: show a multi-line tool command as its first line and its length" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
A follow-up to #48, found by running the new activity log over the real session on #46 (the run that wrote #48).

Tool calls with multi-line scripts came out as one long, unreadable line:

```
🔧 bash: python3 - <<'EOF' p='src/run.ts' s=open(p).read() def rep(a,b): global s assert s.count(a)==1,a s=s.replace(a,b) rep(''…
🔧 bash: cat > /tmp/sess.sh <<'EOF' for r in $(git for-each-ref refs/inspect --format='%(refname)'); do git log --reverse --form…
```

Now they show their first line and how many lines follow:

```
🔧 bash: python3 - <<'EOF' (+97 lines)
🔧 bash: cat > /tmp/sess.sh <<'EOF' (+7 lines)
```

Single-line commands are unchanged. The `↳` group still has the full arguments. The `typescript` tool's `code` gets the same treatment.

`npm run check` passes.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1
